threads.body: `extract_token_details` assumes `input_token_details` / `output_token_details` are dicts; if either key is present but contains a non-dict truthy value, the subsequent `.get(...)` calls will raise at runtime. Since this is instrumentation code, it should be defensive and treat non-dict values as “no details”.

threads.body: `usage_metadata.get("input_tokens"/"output_tokens")` can return non-ints (e.g. `None` or a string) from custom LangChain integrations. That would either store invalid types on the invocation (breaking util-genai metrics/attributes) or raise a `TypeError` later when subtracting `reasoning_tokens`. Coerce to `int` (or default to 0) before assigning/doing arithmetic.
